title: All-day AR battery life
bottleneck: AR glasses carry a fraction of a smartphone's battery yet must power displays, sensors, and spatial compute; current display glasses last 2-4 hours of active use. Bigger batteries add weight that makes glasses unwearable, and wireless tethering to a phone or puck defeats the standalone vision. Energy density of batteries improves only a few percent per year.
why_it_blocks: Without all-day battery, AR glasses are an accessory for demos, not a platform for life. The phone replaced many devices because it lasted the day; AR can't follow until it does too.
current_state: Display-less glasses reach 8+ hours by dropping the display; display models struggle past 3-4 hours. Battery breakthroughs remain the slowest-moving part of the stack. Battery energy density improves only a few percent per year, far slower than the growth in display and compute demands.
